sources.title: Airports (OurAirports) with PCAA annual traffic
sources.publisher: OurAirports (public domain); Pakistan Civil Aviation Authority, Statistics Branch
sources.vintage: OurAirports snapshot at retrieval; PCAA FY 2024-25 (July 2024 - June 2025)
sources.license: OurAirports: public domain; PCAA statistics: published government data (cite PCAA)
used_for: airport icon size by annual passengers
sources.caveats: Selection = OurAirports large_airport + medium_airport + small_airport with scheduled_service=yes; medium_airport includes PAF air bases (flag military=true by name), which carry no civil traffic. Traffic joined by ICAO code (then IATA) to the PCAA FY 2024-25 table; airports absent from the PCAA table have null traffic (not zero). PCAA counts are for airports it operates; ISB 'BBIAP Chaklala' (old Islamabad airport / Nur Khan) is listed separately from Islamabad International (OPIS).

sources.title: 7th Population & Housing Census 2023: district population, growth, religion, mother tongue, literacy
sources.license: Public government statistics
sources.caveats: First digital census (field work Mar-May 2023, reference date 1 Mar 2023). Table 1 population includes head-count-only restricted areas; religion, language, age and literacy (Tables 5-12) cover only fully enumerated population, ~0.4% less nationally, so their totals differ slightly from Table 1. Census 2023 districts are summed onto the COD-AB 2022 frame: Keamari is merged into West Karachi (Karachi district boundaries were redrawn after 2018, so the Karachi split is approximate); Surab = Shaheed Sikandarabad; Lehri = Lehri sub-division (Sibi) + Bhag sub-division (Kachhi), with Sibi and Kachhi reduced accordingly. Growth for merged/derived districts is recomputed from summed 2017 and 2023 counts. Household counts are not published in these tables (only average size). No PBS Census 2023 district tables for Azad Kashmir or Gilgit-Baltistan (left null).

sources.title: Major cities: location, Census 2023 urban-locality population, district
sources.publisher: Pakistan Bureau of Statistics (population); Wikidata contributors (coordinates); OCHA COD-AB (districts)
sources.vintage: 7th Population and Housing Census 2023 (PBS); Wikidata P625 retrieved at build time
sources.license: PBS public release (cite Pakistan Bureau of Statistics); Wikidata CC0
sources.caveats: pop_2023 sums PBS urban localities listed in pop_components: the city's Metropolitan/Municipal Corporation (all tehsil parts) plus named adjoining cantonments where they exist (Lahore, Rawalpindi, Gujranwala, Multan, Hyderabad incl. Qasimabad MC, Peshawar, Quetta, Sargodha, Sialkot, Bahawalpur, Mardan, Okara, Kohat, D.I. Khan, Abbottabad). Karachi = all 42 urban localities of the 7 Karachi Division census districts. Suburban towns with their own MC/TC (e.g. Rohri, Muridke, Taxila, Kotri for Hyderabad) are not added; Wah Cantonment is its own city, separate from Rawalpindi. AJK and GB are not covered by PBS Census 2023 locality tables, so Muzaffarabad, Mirpur, Gilgit and Skardu have null pop_2023 (AJK P&DD publishes only district-level projections). Coordinates are Wikidata's city point (often the historic centre), not a centroid. pcodes uses the COD-AB 2022 frame, in which Keamari is part of West Karachi. Kotri's Wikidata point falls inside COD-AB Hyderabad (PK706) although PBS places Kotri MC in Jamshoro district (Indus-bank boundary edge case).

sources.title: Pakistan subnational administrative boundaries (COD-AB)
sources.license: CC BY-IGO (HDX)
used_for: The 160-district frame every table joins to
sources.caveats: Boundaries follow the UN/OCHA convention and are not an endorsement of any boundary claim. Post-2022 district splits are folded into their 2022 parents.

sources.title: Copernicus DEM GLO-90 (digital surface model)
sources.publisher: European Space Agency / Copernicus, via AWS Open Data Registry
sources.license: Copernicus DEM licence (free use with attribution) © DLR e.V. 2010-2014 and © Airbus 2014-2018
sources.caveats: A surface model: heights include buildings and canopy. 90 m pixels slightly under-read the sharpest summits; the hex 'max' is the highest 90 m pixel in the hex.

sources.title: Agricultural Census 2024: crop area by district (Table 5)
sources.license: PBS public release (cite Pakistan Bureau of Statistics)
sources.caveats: Private farms only; total cropped area counts both Rabi and Kharif seasons. Crop areas are derived from PBS's published percentage shares (1 decimal) x total cropped area, so each is accurate to about +/-0.05% of the district's cropped area. 'Other' includes jowar, barley, tobacco, oilseeds, pulses, vegetables and orchards, yet published shares often sum to <100% (e.g. Ziarat 29.8%, Killa Abdullah 38.3%); the gap is reported as unlisted_area_ha. Census-reported areas are well above Crop Reporting Service / Agricultural Statistics estimates (national cropped area sums to ~33.5 Mha, wheat ~14.5 Mha), so use them for relative crop mix, not as official crop-area statistics. Because Rabi wheat is counted, wheat is the 'dominant' crop almost everywhere. No production figures (prod_t null). PBS reports 'Cholistan Area' as a separate unit (desert tracts of Bahawalpur/Bahawalnagar/Rahim Yar Khan); it is kept unassigned. Keamari is summed into West Karachi, Surab = Shaheed Sikandarabad. No AJK/GB tables.

sources.title: Cultural mosaic: Sufi shrines, craft hubs and cricket grounds
sources.license: Wikidata CC0; Wikipedia text CC BY-SA 4.0
sources.caveats: Curated list from the living pakistan brief, not a ranking. Shrine points are the shrine's Wikidata item where one exists, otherwise the town of the shrine (facts.coord_from) and so are approximate. Craft pins mark the hub town, not a workshop, and are included only when the cited Wikipedia article mentions the craft (facts.evidence holds the sentence); unverified crafts are dropped. Stadium capacity is the current English Wikipedia infobox value (Wikidata P1083 kept alongside; the two can disagree after renovations). Arbab Niaz Stadium appears under its current enwiki title, Imran Khan Cricket Stadium.

sources.title: Economic Census 2023: establishments and workforce by PSIC section
sources.license: PBS public release (cite Pakistan Bureau of Statistics)
sources.caveats: Workplace-based count of establishments (shops, offices, factories, schools, mosques, cattle farms) and persons working in them; major PSIC sections only. Section 'X' is PBS's unclassified 'Others'. No district tables for Azad Kashmir or Gilgit-Baltistan. EC districts are summed onto COD-AB 2022 districts (e.g. Keamari into West Karachi, Surab = Shaheed Sikandarabad). Lehri has no separate EC table. A few Punjab district blocks omit sections that are zero.

sources.title: Civilisation eras and era-defining sites of Pakistan
sources.license: Wikipedia text CC BY-SA 4.0; Wikidata CC0
sources.caveats: Era boundaries are conventional and overlap (e.g. Mehrgarh runs into the Early Harappan; Mughal rule's nominal end in 1857 postdates the Sikh/British takeover of Punjab and Sindh). Each era boundary year was checked against the cited Wikipedia article text; 'Sikh & British' starts with the Sikh Empire (1799). Archaeological dates are approximate and contested (Mehrgarh's earliest occupation is given as 7000 BCE or 5250 BCE). A site's year is its founding/construction/completion/event year as described in facts.year_note; century-only dates are placed at the century midpoint. Sites with no verifiable year have year null. Coordinates are Wikidata P625 (one representative point; facts.coord_src says otherwise).

sources.title: ESA WorldCover 10 m 2021 v200
sources.publisher: European Space Agency (ESA WorldCover consortium), AWS Open Data
sources.license: CC BY 4.0 — © ESA WorldCover project 2021 / Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data (2021)
used_for: Farmland / Forest / Desert / Glacier / Built-up lenses
sources.caveats: Read from the COG 1/16 overview (~160 m), then aggregated to 20 km hexes: small orchards, villages and narrow canals are blurred into their surroundings.

sources.title: Gridded GDP (PPP), MODELLED -- Kummu et al.
sources.publisher: Kummu, Kosonen & Masoumzadeh Sayyar (Aalto University), Scientific Data 12:178 (2025); Zenodo v4
sources.vintage: 2024 band of the 1990-2024 dataset (Zenodo record 18429133, published 2026-03-13)
sources.license: CC-BY-4.0
used_for: Gold yield (modelled GDP) for hexes and districts
sources.caveats: MODELLED, NOT OFFICIAL. Pakistan has no official district GDP; this grid downscales reported national/provincial GDP per capita to admin-2 units and multiplies by gridded population, so it mostly mirrors where people live, scaled by provincial income. 30 arc-second (~0.9 km) cells; district totals sum cells whose centres fall inside COD-AB 2022 polygons. Units: 2021 international dollars (PPP).

sources.title: Natural hazards of Pakistan: earthquakes, faults, heat, glacial floods, 2022 floods, EM-DAT
sources.publisher: USGS ComCat; GEM Foundation; CRED EM-DAT via HDX; NDMA Pakistan; World Bank/GoP PDNA; WMO; UNDP/GCF; Wikipedia/Wikidata
sources.vintage: ComCat 1900-2026-11; EM-DAT profile 2026-11-25; NDMA SITREP 158 (18 Nov 2022); PDNA Oct 2022
sources.license: USGS public domain; GEM GAF CC BY-SA 4.0; EM-DAT (CRED/UCLouvain) non-commercial with attribution; NDMA/PDNA/GCF public reports; Wikipedia CC BY-SA; Wikidata CC0
used_for: Hazards layer: earthquake dots and fault lines
Surprise Me: heat records (Jacobabad, Turbat, Mohenjo-daro)
sources.caveats: ComCat completeness varies hugely over time (pre-1973 entries are mostly ISC-GEM M~5.5+); the box includes Afghanistan, Iran, India and Tajikistan, pcode is set only for points inside Pakistan. Death tolls of historic quakes are ranges from Wikipedia infoboxes and differ between sources (Wikidata values are given separately). Heat records mix WMO-verified (Turbat) and PMD/Wikipedia station values; Wikipedia climate boxes give monthly extremes without dates. The EM-DAT HDX profile only covers 2000 onwards; damage is as published (USD, original and CPI-adjusted). GLOF sites are a short, referenced list, not an inventory (ICIMOD inventory not openly downloadable). Faults are simplified at ~0.01 deg and are not suitable for site hazard assessment.

sources.title: Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) by district
sources.publisher: Ministry of Planning, Development & Special Initiatives (Planning Commission), with UNICEF/UNDP and OPHI
sources.license: Government of Pakistan publication (cite MoPD&SI / OPHI)
used_for: Poverty lens (MPI, headcount H, intensity A)
sources.caveats: Official national MPI (15 indicators; poor if deprived in >=1/3 weighted indicators). District estimates from PSLM samples have wide confidence intervals (e.g. Kohlu, Sherani). 2019-20 does not cover AJK, Gilgit-Baltistan or a few Balochistan districts; four of those use 2014-15 values (field year='2014-15') and are not strictly comparable. Districts split after the survey inherit the parent's value (inherited_from). H and A are percentages.

sources.title: Natural Earth 1:10m land, lakes and countries (v5.1)
sources.license: Public domain
sources.caveats: 1:10m generalisation; Pakistan's own outline comes from COD-AB.

sources.title: Seaports and harbours
sources.publisher: US NGA (World Port Index, Pub 150); Natural Earth; Finance Division, Govt of Pakistan (Pakistan Economic Survey 2024-25); Wikidata
sources.vintage: WPI copy of 2024-05 (RIMES mirror); cargo FY 2023-24 (PES 2024-25)
sources.license: WPI: US Government work (public domain); Natural Earth: public domain; PES: government publication (cite); Wikidata: CC0
used_for: port icon size by cargo tonnage
sources.caveats: WPI lists only three Pakistani ports (Karachi, Muhammad Bin Qasim, Gwadar). The official NGA server returned 503, so the CSV is a 2024-05 copy hosted by RIMES CKAN. Minor harbours (Pasni fish harbour — placed at the Pasni town point because the harbour item has no coordinates, Ormara naval base, Keti Bandar, Gadani ship-breaking) are placed from Wikidata coordinates and have no tonnage. Cargo is total imports+exports for FY 2023-24 (July-June) from the Pakistan Economic Survey 2024-25; Gwadar's figure appears only as an unreadable chart in that PDF and is left null. Port points lie on water, so pcode falls back to the nearest district within ~10 km (pcode_method='nearest').

sources.title: Power plants (WRI Global Power Plant Database + curated post-2018 supplement)
sources.publisher: World Resources Institute et al. (GPPD v1.3.0); supplement: CPEC Authority, Wikidata, Wikipedia, OpenStreetMap
sources.license: GPPD: CC BY 4.0; Wikidata: CC0; Wikipedia: CC BY-SA 4.0; OSM: ODbL
used_for: power plant points sized by capacity and coloured by fuel
sources.caveats: GPPD lists only 62 Pakistani plants and is stale (no Thar coal, Neelum-Jhelum, Karot, K-2/K-3, RLNG plants). A short supplement (rows with src_detail='supplement') adds major plants commissioned since ~2018, each with a reference URL; Tarbela 4th/5th extensions are listed as separate rows on top of GPPD's 3,478 MW Tarbela figure. GPPD coordinates for some IPPs are approximate (several share one point). Small wind/solar IPPs after 2018 are not added. Capacity is nameplate MW as stated by the reference, not NEPRA dependable capacity.

sources.title: OpenStreetMap Pakistan extract: roads, railways, canals, barrages
sources.license: ODbL 1.0 (Open Database License), (c) OpenStreetMap contributors
sources.caveats: Crowd-sourced; completeness and ref tagging vary. Motorways are taken from M-<n> refs on motorway/trunk/primary ways plus highway=motorway ways with other or no refs; national highways from N-<n> refs on trunk/primary ways only (untagged or differently tagged sections are missing). Lines are simplified (~0.01 deg) and dual carriageways/double tracks collapsed, so lengths are approximate. Geofabrik's extract boundary includes AJK/Gilgit-Baltistan and slivers of neighbouring countries; features there have pcode null. Barrages/dams are name-matched points. Rivers are name-matched waterway=river ways (braided channels collapsed; only the part inside the extract, so trans-boundary rivers are truncated).

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Sites and Tentative List: Pakistan
sources.license: UNESCO WHC data (c) UNESCO, reuse with attribution; Wikidata CC0
sources.caveats: Inscribed sites and criteria come from the WHC XML list. Tentative-list entries carry the year of submission, not inscription; their coordinates come from the WHC tentative-list page or Wikidata and may be null when neither gives a point. Serial properties are pinned at one representative point.

sources.title: Universities and tech hubs (OpenAlex research output)
sources.license: OpenAlex CC0; Wikidata CC0
sources.caveats: RULE: the top 15 Pakistani education institutions by OpenAlex works_count (all-time indexed publications), taking at most 2 per city (OpenAlex geo.city); lower-ranked ones in a full city are skipped. Research output is a proxy for prominence, not enrolment, quality or R&D spend; medical colleges and multi-campus systems are counted as OpenAlex groups them. Tech-hub tag is a curated list of engineering/computing flagships (NUST, LUMS, FAST-NUCES, GIKI, COMSATS, PIEAS, UET, NED, ITU, MUET, Air University) shown even outside the top 15. Coordinates are Wikidata P625 campus points; where missing or more than 25 km from the OpenAlex city, the Wikipedia coordinate, else the OpenAlex city centroid (facts.coord_src); if that centroid is itself >25 km from the COD-AB centroid of the same-named district, the district centroid is used.

sources.title: UNOSAT satellite-detected flood water, Pakistan 2022 (VIIRS extent + weekly flood evolution by district)
sources.vintage: Cumulative extent 1 Jul – 31 Aug 2022; weekly evolution Aug – Dec 2022 (release 3 Jan 2023)
sources.license: UNOSAT products: free for humanitarian and non-commercial use with attribution
used_for: 2022 Mega-Flood lens (share of each hex's land under water)
sources.caveats: Satellite analysis, not field validated. Cloud cover hides some water in some weeks. The playback spreads each district's weekly flooded area over that district's cumulative footprint hexes — the weekly *district totals* are UNOSAT's; their placement inside a district is approximate. The 1 Jul – 31 Aug VIIRS composite also picks up flooded rice paddies (Punjab rice belt, e.g. Sialkot); living pakistan district headlines therefore use the peak of the cloud-free weekly windows (from 25 Aug), with the monthly maximum shown separately.

sources.title: Indus Basin dams, barrages and headworks
sources.publisher: Wikidata; English Wikipedia (infoboxes citing WAPDA / Punjab & Sindh Irrigation Depts); OpenStreetMap (location cross-check)
sources.license: Wikidata: CC0; Wikipedia: CC BY-SA 4.0; OSM: ODbL
used_for: Indus Waters Treaty western/eastern river lens
sources.caveats: The list of structures is curated; every numeric fact is parsed from the cited Wikipedia infobox (or Wikidata) and is null when the reference doesn't give it. design_discharge_cusecs is the spillway / flood design discharge given in the infobox, not canal command capacity. Storage values are the infobox's design figures (often original, before sedimentation). Year = infobox 'opening' (null for structures under construction). Where the Wikidata point is more than 5 km from the named OSM structure (or missing), the OSM point is used (coord_src).

sources.title: Natural & cultural wonders and national parks
sources.publisher: Wikidata / Wikipedia (curated list); UNEP-WCMC & IUCN Protected Planet (WDPCA)
sources.vintage: Wikidata/Wikipedia as retrieved 2026-11; WDPCA v5 (HDX unep_wdpca_pak)
sources.license: Wikidata CC0; Wikipedia text CC BY-SA 4.0; WDPCA (c) UNEP-WCMC & IUCN, non-commercial terms
sources.caveats: PUBLISHED RULE: wonders are a curated, editorial list, not a ranking. Natural: all five 8,000 m peaks in Pakistan-administered territory (K2, Nanga Parbat, Gasherbrum I, Broad Peak, Gasherbrum II), plus Rakaposhi and Tirich Mir (highest of the Hindu Kush); four major Karakoram glaciers (Siachen, Baltoro, Biafo, Batura); and 19 signature landscapes (Deosai, Hingol incl. Princess of Hope & Kund Malir, Khunjerab Pass, Attabad, Saiful Muluk, Shandur, Indus Delta, Thar, Cholistan, Khewra, Fairy Meadows, Kalash valleys, Astola). Cultural: national symbols and Mughal/Sikh/colonial/princely monuments (most on UNESCO's Tentative List) plus Harappa and Mehrgarh, and Quaid-e-Azam Solar Park as a modern outlier. The six UNESCO World Heritage properties are in the unesco layer, not repeated here. Numeric facts are Wikidata values (units normalised); null when Wikidata has none. Siachen lies in a disputed area; Thar, Cholistan and the Indus Delta are extensive regions pinned at one Wikidata point (pcode may be null if that point is outside Pakistan). National parks: every WDPCA record designated 'National Park' (polygon or point layer) with reported area; WDPCA areas are as reported by the government and may differ from GIS areas.

sources.title: WorldPop Global2 population 2025, Pakistan, constrained 1 km (R2025A v1)
sources.license: CC BY 4.0
used_for: Spreading each district's Census 2023 population across its hexes
sources.caveats: Modelled gridded population. For the 136 districts with Census 2023 tables, hex values are rescaled so each district sums to its census total; AJK and Gilgit-Baltistan show WorldPop 2025 directly.
